newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse to find way to better times.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse to find way to better times.

text.p: Friday's market in leading Belgian shares will focus on special situations amid a dearth of major U.S. economic indicators and the likely absence of market moving EMU news, dealers said on Thursday.

Indications from Wall Street where the Dow Jones was up 23 points after the close of trade here allowed for hopes that the Brussels' Bel-20 index would break a three-day run of losses and go back to its longer-term uptrend, they said.
Firmness on Wall Street helped the Bel-20 pare most of the day's losses. It closed down just 1.95 points at 2,345.60 after having lost 12.48 points on Wednesday and 27.37 on Tuesday.
Late afternoon dollar weakness, however, injected a note of caution.
Dealers said that any moves would occur in a much becalmed climate after the choppiness of recent weeks in the wake of worries Germany and France might not make it into EMU.
They added the bourse as a rule calmed down in the holiday months of July and August after bouts of action during the preceeding annual dividend payout period.

Dealers said the focus would now swing back to sound fundamentals -- low interest rates, muted inflation and an expected pick-up in growth -- and to special situations surrounding possible takeovers, mergers and demergers.

Kredietbank lost 125 francs to 14,500 as speculation it would merge with Rabobank of the Netherlands and/or Belgian CERA Bank faded further into the background. The share also remained under pressure from a downgrade by Merrill Lynch, dealers said.
Colruyt dipped 150 francs to 16,500 as buying in the wake of news the retailer might split up its computer unit Dolmen with the aim of a possible sale or partnership of one part dried up.
"We need some actual news on Dolmen for buyers to come back," a trader said.
In the same sector GIB benefitted from talk its partner search for some of its businesses, particularly its DIY outlets, might hot up. The share added 25 francs at 1,720.
Delhaize, the third retailer in the Bel-20, put on 15 francs at 1,835 as shares in its U.S. unit Food Lion appeared to have found back to the uptrend.

Elsewhere, chemical share Solvay shed 575 francs at 21,450 as analysts turned cautious, saying the outlook for plastics and peroxides was still tough. Dealers said the share might lose another 500 or 1,000 francs before buyers would return.
Finally, dealers said, the market was wondering how much further steel wire and cord firm Bekaert would rise before "catch-up" buying would dry up.
The stock rose 400 francs to 22,525, for a total gain of 1,475 francs since June 13, as investors returned after having ignored it in the wake of two profit warnings issued last year.

One trader said Bekaert had also lagged the Bel-20 index in the past eight weeks. At current levels the share was practically unchanged, while the index had gained over 100 points over that period, making Bekaert "something for stock-pickers."
